You went 3 times last month. That's $83 a visit. Nobody's saying cancel. We're saying that's the number, and it's yours to decide what it's worth.

items.n: Boutique class membership (Barry's, SoulCycle, F45, Orangetheory)
items.t: Classes get people through the door more reliably than a gym floor does, which is the real reason to pay for them. If you're going, keep. If you're not, the number is $200 a month for a good intention.
You've got two memberships and last month you used one of them. Keep that one. $150 a month back, and nothing about your training changes.
There are 7 credits on that pack and the last one was used in June. If they expire, that's money gone; if they don't, book them before buying anything else. Either way this comes off the count.

items.n: Fitness app subscription (Peloton app, Apple Fitness+, Ladder)
items.t: Last opened six weeks ago and still billing. $25 a month back, and you can always resubscribe the week you actually want it.

items.n: Recovery studio membership (Restore, Remedy Place, Othership)
items.t: The sauna and the plunge in there are testable, and worth testing. The rest of the menu mostly isn't. If you're going twice a week, we'll test what we can. If you went once last month, that's $250 for one visit.

items.n: Sauna or cold-plunge studio when you own one at home
items.t: You've got a plunge in the garage and a studio membership for the same thing. The garage one is free from here. $150 a month back.
Three credits banked and the last visit was in July. Use them, or stop the billing until you will. Massage isn't the problem; the auto-renew is.
If most of it gets eaten, this is a fine way to spend $400. If half of it goes in the bin, that's $200 a month on food you didn't want. You'd know which.
Last opened in August, still billing. $15 a month back until the week you want it again.
Two subscriptions for the same ten minutes a day. Keep the one you actually open. $15 a month back.
Standard care. Not ours to rate.
You're buying salt and sugar twice. Keep the packets if you sweat hard; the sports drink is the same thing with more sugar. $40 a month back.
There's about 2 g of collagen in each of these. The trials that found anything used 10. Same ingredient as the powder, one fifth of the dose, twice the price. $40 a month back.

If you only keep one thing on this list, keep this one. A ring can't see it, and it doesn't matter; the evidence is as strong as evidence gets.
Well proven, and we can't see it, so a weekly skin rating is the honest way to watch it. Keep.

If the bottle is clear or the serum has gone orange, the vitamin C is already gone. If it's a proper L-ascorbic acid formula, keep it and rate your skin weekly. That's $60 a month riding on the packaging.

items.n: Retinol or retinoid plus exfoliating acid on the same nights
items.t: These two on the same night are fighting each other, and your skin is where the fight happens. Alternate nights and you get the same result with less redness. If you'd rather simplify, the acid is the one to drop.

items.n: Two exfoliants (scrub plus acid, or two acids)
items.t: One of these is doing the job and the other is doing damage. Keep the acid, drop the scrub. $25 a month back and calmer skin.
This step made sense with the harsh soaps of forty years ago. With a gentle cleanser and a serum, it's doing the serum's job for a second time. $25 a month back and one fewer bottle.

items.n: Multiple hydrating serums (two hyaluronic acid products)
items.t: Two bottles of the same ingredient. Keep the one you like the feel of. $50 a month back.

items.n: Eye cream (when you already use a moisturiser)
items.t: Read both labels. If the eye cream has an ingredient your moisturiser doesn't, keep it. If it's the same list in a smaller jar, that's $45 a month for the jar.

items.n: Facial plus at-home LED plus microcurrent (all three)
items.t: Three things, one face, and only the LED has real evidence behind it. Pick one. If it's the facials, that's fine; just know the devices are then in a drawer costing $60 a month between them.

items.g: professional skin treatments, at-home skin devices
items.t: Any lift from this is temporary, and the studies are the company's. If you use it and like it, that's a real reason. If it's in a drawer, it comes off the count.
Costs nothing, feels nice, and the de-puffing is real for a few hours. Keep it if it's yours.

items.watch: Overnight HRV; time to fall asleep
items.t: It's in the garage. When did you last get in it? If the answer is 'a while', that's the verdict, and no experiment is needed.

items.n: Unlisted device you haven't used in 30 days
items.t: You bought it, you tried it, and it's been in a drawer since spring. That's a verdict you reached on your own. It comes off the count, and if it has a resale value, that's the only number left.

items.n: Unlisted subscription you're still paying for
items.t: Still billing, last used over a month ago. That's the whole verdict. Cancel it, and resubscribe the week you want it back.
